at fejle.explanation: "At fejle" means "to fail". To say a plan did not work, use it with the plan: "Planen fejlede" (The plan failed). To ask what is wrong with someone's health, use it in the question: "Hvad fejler du?" (What is wrong with you?)

at fejre.explanation: "At fejre" means "to celebrate". To say which holiday you celebrate, put it after the verb: "Vi fejrer jul sammen" (We celebrate Christmas together).

at feste.explanation: "At feste" means "to party". It is the verb for the noun "en fest" (a party). To say who you party with, add "med" (with): "Jeg fester med mine venner" (I party with my friends).

at fikse.explanation: "At fikse" means "to fix". To promise someone you will fix a problem, say: "Jeg skal nok fikse det" (I will fix it, do not worry).

at filme.explanation: "At filme" means "to film". It is the verb for the noun "en film" (a movie). To say who you film, put the person after the verb: "Jeg filmer min datter" (I film my daughter).

at finansiere.explanation: "At finansiere" means "to finance". To say who pays for something, put the payer first: "Staten finansierer broen" (The state finances the bridge).

at finde.explanation: "At finde" means "to find". To give your opinion, use it as English does in "I find it difficult": "Jeg finder det svært" (I find it difficult).

at finde på.explanation: "At finde på" means "to come up with". To say you invent a game or a plan, use it: "Vi fandt på en leg" (We came up with a game). Do not mix it up with "at finde" (to find), which is for something that already exists: "Jeg finder nøglen" (I find the key).

at finde ud af.explanation: "At finde ud af" means "to find out / figure out". To say you learn a fact, use it with a question word: "Jeg finder ud af, hvornår toget kører" (I find out when the train leaves). Do not mix it up with "at finde på" (to come up with), which is for ideas: "Vi finder på en løsning" (We come up with a solution).

at finde vej.explanation: "At finde vej" means "to find one's way". The opposite is "at fare vild" (to get lost). To say you got lost, use its past tense: "Vi for vild i skoven" (We got lost in the forest).

at fjerne.explanation: "At fjerne" means "to remove". It is built from "fjern" (distant). The same word is in "en fjernbetjening" (a remote control).

at flirte.explanation: "At flirte" means "to flirt". To say who you flirt with, add "med" (with): "Hun flirter med bartenderen" (She flirts with the bartender).

at flyde.explanation: "At flyde" means "to float / flow". When you talk about water moving along, it means "to flow": "Floden flyder ud i havet" (The river flows into the sea). When you talk about something that stays on top of a liquid, it means "to float": "Olie flyder ovenpå vand" (Oil floats on top of water).

at flygte.explanation: "At flygte" means "to flee". To say where someone flees to, add "til" (to): "De flygtede til Sverige" (They fled to Sweden).

at flytte.explanation: "At flytte" means "to move", as in moving house. To say you move a thing from one place to another, put the thing after the verb: "Kan du flytte bilen?" (Can you move the car?)

at flytte ind.explanation: "At flytte ind" means "to move in". It is "at flytte" (to move) plus "ind" (in). To say you move a thing instead, leave out "ind": "Jeg flytter bordet" (I move the table).

at flytte sammen.explanation: "At flytte sammen" means "to move in together". It is "at flytte" (to move) plus "sammen" (together). To say who you move in with, add "med" (with): "Jeg flytter sammen med min kæreste" (I am moving in with my boyfriend or girlfriend).

at flytte sig.explanation: "At flytte sig" means "to move (oneself)". To ask someone to step aside, say: "Kan du flytte dig?" (Can you move over?) To say you change homes, leave out "sig" (oneself): "Vi flytter til Aarhus" (We are moving to Aarhus).

at flytte ud.explanation: "At flytte ud" means "to move out". The opposite is "at flytte ind" (to move in). To say when you move in, say: "Vi flytter ind i morgen" (We are moving in tomorrow).

at flyve.explanation: "At flyve" means "to fly". To say time passes quickly, use it for time: "Tiden flyver" (Time flies).

at flå.explanation: "At flå" means "to rip / skin". When you tear a package open, use it: "Han flåede pakken op" (He ripped the package open). When you take the skin off an animal, use it: "Kokken flår kaninen" (The cook skins the rabbit). When a business charges far too much, use it: "Hotellet flår turisterne" (The hotel rips off the tourists).

at flække.explanation: "At flække" means "to split". To say what you split, put it after the verb: "Han flækker brænde" (He splits firewood).

at fnise.explanation: "At fnise" means "to giggle". To describe children giggling, say: "Børnene fnisede bag bogen" (The children giggled behind the book).

at fodre.explanation: "At fodre" means "to feed". It is the verb for the noun "et foder" (animal feed). To say what you feed an animal with, add "med" (with): "Jeg fodrer hestene med hø" (I feed the horses with hay).

at fokusere.explanation: "At fokusere" means "to focus". To say what you focus on, add "på" (on): "Jeg fokuserer på arbejdet" (I focus on the work).

at folde.explanation: "At folde" means "to fold". To say you put your hands together, use it with the hands: "at folde hænderne" (to fold your hands). To say you fold a sheet of paper, say: "Hun folder papiret" (She folds the paper).

at forandre.explanation: "At forandre" means "to change". To say you replace one thing with another, use "at skifte" (to switch) instead: "Jeg skifter job" (I am changing jobs).

at forandre sig.explanation: "At forandre sig" means "to change". To say a place or a person has become different, use "sig" (oneself): "Byen har forandret sig" (The city has changed). To say you change something, leave out "sig": "Han forandrer planen" (He changes the plan).

at forankre.explanation: "At forankre" means "to anchor". It is built from "et anker" (an anchor). To say where an idea or decision is rooted, add "i" (in): "Beslutningen er forankret i ledelsen" (The decision is anchored in the management).

at forbedre.explanation: "At forbedre" means "to improve". It is built from "bedre" (better). To say something gets better without anyone working on it, use "at blive bedre" (to get better): "Vejret bliver bedre" (The weather is getting better).

at forbeholde.explanation: "At forbeholde" means "to reserve", as in keeping something for certain people only. To say who a seat is kept for, say: "Pladsen er forbeholdt gæster" (The seat is reserved for guests). To say you keep a right for yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Vi forbeholder os retten til at ændre prisen" (We reserve the right to change the price).

at forberede sig.explanation: "At forberede sig" means "to prepare oneself". To say you prepare a thing instead of yourself, leave out "sig" (oneself): "Hun forbereder et møde" (She prepares a meeting).

at forbinde.explanation: "At forbinde" means "to connect". To say what you connect something to, add "med" (with): "Jeg forbinder printeren med computeren" (I connect the printer to the computer). When you link one thing with another in your mind, it means "to associate": "Jeg forbinder sommer med is" (I associate summer with ice cream).

at forblive.explanation: "At forblive" means "to remain". To say what someone stays, put it after the verb: "Vi forbliver venner" (We remain friends). To say someone becomes something new, use "at blive" (to become) instead: "Hun bliver direktør" (She becomes director).

at forbruge.explanation: "At forbruge" means "to consume". To say what a household uses up, use it with the supply: "Vi forbruger meget vand" (We consume a lot of water). To say you eat a meal, use "at spise" (to eat) instead: "Jeg spiser frokost" (I eat lunch).

at forbyde.explanation: "At forbyde" means "to forbid / ban". To say a government bans something, put the thing after the verb: "Regeringen forbyder plastikposer" (The government bans plastic bags). To say something is not allowed, use "forbudt" (forbidden): "Det er forbudt at ryge her" (Smoking is forbidden here).

at fordele.explanation: "At fordele" means "to distribute". To say who shares the money, use "mellem" (between): "Vi fordeler pengene mellem børnene" (We distribute the money between the children).

at fordoble.explanation: "At fordoble" means "to double". To say a number doubles by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Antallet fordobler sig hvert år" (The number doubles every year).

at fordybe sig.explanation: "At fordybe sig" means "to immerse oneself". It is built from "dyb" (deep). To say what you are immersed in, add "i" (in): "Han fordyber sig i sin forskning" (He immerses himself in his research).

at foregive.explanation: "At foregive" means "to pretend". To say someone pretends to be something, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Han foregav at være syg" (He pretended to be sick). To say the same with a full sentence, use "at lade som om" (to act as if): "Han lod som om, han var syg" (He pretended he was sick).

at foregå.explanation: "At foregå" means "to take place / happen". To say where an event takes place, name the place after the verb: "Mødet foregår i konferencelokalet" (The meeting takes place in the conference room). Its forms start with "det" (it), because the verb is used about events, not about people.

at forene.explanation: "At forene" means "to unite". To say you bring two countries together, say: "Vi vil forene de to lande" (We want to unite the two countries). When you combine two things in your life, it means "to combine": "Hun forener arbejde og familie" (She combines work and family).

at forenkle.explanation: "At forenkle" means "to simplify". It is built from "enkel" (simple). To say you make rules simpler, use it with the rules: "Vi forenkler reglerne" (We simplify the rules).

at foreslå.explanation: "At foreslå" means "to suggest". To suggest a thing, put it straight after the verb: "Jeg foreslår en anden dag" (I suggest another day).

at forestille sig.explanation: "At forestille sig" means "to imagine". To say you cannot picture something, say: "Jeg kan ikke forestille mig det" (I cannot imagine that).

at forestå.explanation: "At forestå" means "to be in charge of / lie ahead". When someone runs a department or a project, it means "to be in charge of": "Hun forestår afdelingen" (She is in charge of the department). When something is coming, it means "to lie ahead": "Der forestår en svær tid" (A hard time lies ahead).

at foretage.explanation: "At foretage" means "to make / carry out". To say you make a change, say: "Vi foretager en ændring" (We make a change). To say you make a call, say: "Jeg foretager et opkald" (I make a call). To say you make a cake, use "at lave" (to make) instead: "Jeg laver en kage" (I am making a cake).

at foretrække.explanation: "At foretrække" means "to prefer". To say what someone prefers to do, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Hun foretrækker at gå" (She prefers to walk). To name the option you like less, add "frem for" (over): "Jeg foretrækker hunde frem for katte" (I prefer dogs to cats).

at forfalde.explanation: "At forfalde" means "to fall due / decay". When a payment reaches its deadline, it means "to fall due": "Fakturaen forfalder om fjorten dage" (The invoice falls due in fourteen days). When a building falls into ruin, it means "to decay": "Huset forfalder" (The house is falling apart).

at forfatte.explanation: "At forfatte" means "to compose", as in writing a text. It is the verb for "en forfatter" (a writer). To say you write a letter with care, say: "Hun forfattede et brev til ministeren" (She composed a letter to the minister).

at forfremme.explanation: "At forfremme" means "to promote", as in moving a person up to a better job: "Chefen forfremmede hende" (The boss promoted her). To promote a product, use "at markedsføre" (to market) instead: "Vi markedsfører den nye cykel" (We market the new bike).

at forfølge.explanation: "At forfølge" means "to pursue / persecute". When you follow a goal, it means "to pursue": "Hun forfølger sin drøm" (She pursues her dream). When a ruler treats people cruelly for their views, it means "to persecute": "Regimet forfølger sine kritikere" (The regime persecutes its critics).

at forføre.explanation: "At forføre" means "to seduce". It is built from "for" and "at føre" (to lead). To say someone tried to win a person over, say: "Han forsøgte at forføre hende" (He tried to seduce her).

at forhandle.explanation: "At forhandle" means "to negotiate". To name the topic, add "om" (about): "Vi forhandler om prisen" (We negotiate the price). Do not mix it up with "en forhandler" (a dealer), who sells goods: "Jeg køber bilen hos en forhandler" (I buy the car from a dealer).

at forhindre.explanation: "At forhindre" means "to prevent". To say what someone was stopped from doing, add "i at" (from) before the verb: "Regnen forhindrede os i at gå" (The rain stopped us from going).

at forhøre sig.explanation: "At forhøre sig" means "to inquire". To name the topic you ask about, add "om" (about): "Jeg forhører mig om åbningstiderne" (I am inquiring about the opening hours). Without "sig" (oneself), "at forhøre" means to interrogate: "Politiet forhører den mistænkte" (The police interrogate the suspect).

at forklare.explanation: "At forklare" means "to explain". To say who you explain something to, use "for" after the thing: "Kan du forklare det for mig?" (Can you explain it to me?)

at forklæde sig.explanation: "At forklæde sig" means "to disguise oneself". To say what you disguise yourself as, add "som" (as): "Hun forklædte sig som tjener" (She disguised herself as a waiter).

at forkorte.explanation: "At forkorte" means "to shorten". To say you make a meeting shorter, say: "Vi forkorter mødet" (We shorten the meeting). When you shorten a word, it means "to abbreviate", and the result is "en forkortelse" (an abbreviation).

at forkæle.explanation: "At forkæle" means "to spoil (pamper)". When you treat someone to nice things, say: "Jeg vil forkæle dig i dag" (I want to pamper you today). To say a child gets too much and expects it, use the form "forkælet": "Børnene er forkælede" (The children are spoiled).

at forlade.explanation: "At forlade" means "to leave". To say you leave a place, put the place after it: "Hun forlod huset klokken 8" (She left the house at 8). To say you leave a person, put the person after it: "Hun forlod ham" (She left him). To say you are simply going away, use "at gå" (to go): "Jeg går nu" (I am leaving now).

at forlange.explanation: "At forlange" means "to demand". To say what someone demands, put it after the verb: "Han forlangte sine penge tilbage" (He demanded his money back). To say someone asks for something politely, use "at bede om" (to ask for) instead: "Jeg beder om regningen" (I ask for the bill).

at forlove sig.explanation: "At forlove sig" means "to get engaged". To name the person you get engaged to, add "med" (with): "Hun forlovede sig med Peter i sommer" (She got engaged to Peter last summer).

at forlænge.explanation: "At forlænge" means "to extend". To say you make a permit last longer, say: "Jeg forlænger mit visum" (I extend my visa). To say you make a thing longer, put it after the verb: "Vi forlænger bordet" (We make the table longer).

at forløbe.explanation: "At forløbe" means "to proceed / go". To say how an event went, add a word for how: "Festen forløb roligt" (The party went calmly). Its forms start with "det" (it), because the verb is used about events, not about people.

at formidle.explanation: "At formidle" means "to convey / mediate". When you pass knowledge from one person to others, it means "to convey": "Læreren formidler viden til eleverne" (The teacher conveys knowledge to the students). When you arrange something between two sides, it means "to mediate": "Hun formidler en aftale mellem de to firmaer" (She mediates a deal between the two companies).

at formindske.explanation: "At formindske" means "to reduce". To say you cut costs, say: "Vi formindsker udgifterne" (We reduce the costs). Danish also has the shorter "at mindske" (to lessen): "Vi mindsker risikoen" (We lessen the risk).

at formode.explanation: "At formode" means "to suppose / presume". To say what you assume, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg formoder, at han kommer snart" (I presume he is coming soon).

at formulere.explanation: "At formulere" means "to formulate". To ask someone to word a question another way, say: "Kan du formulere spørgsmålet anderledes?" (Can you word the question differently?)

at fornemme.explanation: "At fornemme" means "to sense". To say you feel that something is wrong, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg fornemmer, at noget er galt" (I sense that something is wrong).

at forny.explanation: "At forny" means "to renew". It is built from "ny" (new). To say you make a document valid again, say: "Jeg skal forny mit pas" (I have to renew my passport).

at fornægte.explanation: "At fornægte" means "to deny", as in refusing to accept that something is real. To say someone refuses to accept his feelings, say: "Han fornægter sine følelser" (He denies his feelings). To say you deny doing something, use "at nægte" (to deny) instead: "Jeg nægter at have taget pengene" (I deny taking the money).

at fornærme.explanation: "At fornærme" means "to offend". To say you did not mean to hurt someone, say: "Jeg ville ikke fornærme dig" (I did not mean to offend you).

at forpligte.explanation: "At forpligte" means "to commit / oblige". When an agreement ties someone to something, it means "to oblige": "Kontrakten forpligter firmaet" (The contract obliges the company). When you promise to do something yourself, add "sig" (oneself) and it means "to commit": "Jeg forpligter mig til at komme" (I commit myself to coming).

at forråde.explanation: "At forråde" means "to betray". To say someone turns on a friend, put the friend after the verb: "Han forrådte sin ven" (He betrayed his friend). When something gives a person away, it also fits: "Hans smil forrådte ham" (His smile gave him away).

at forsikre.explanation: "At forsikre" means "to assure / insure". When you tell someone that something is certain, it means "to assure": "Jeg forsikrer dig om, at det er sikkert" (I assure you it is safe). When you buy cover against damage, it means "to insure": "Vi forsikrer bilen" (We insure the car). The cover itself is "en forsikring" (an insurance).

at forsinke.explanation: "At forsinke" means "to delay". To say a train is late, use the form "forsinket" (delayed): "Toget er forsinket" (The train is delayed).

at forske.explanation: "At forske" means "to research". To name the subject, add "i" (in): "Hun har forsket i kræft i ti år" (She has researched cancer for ten years).

at forskrække.explanation: "At forskrække" means "to frighten". To say you gave someone a sudden shock, say: "Du forskrækkede mig" (You frightened me). To say you got a fright, use "at blive forskrækket" (to get a fright): "Jeg blev forskrækket" (I got a fright).

at forskyde.explanation: "At forskyde" means "to shift / displace". To say a time moves to a different point, use it for time: "Vi forskyder mødet en time" (We shift the meeting by an hour). In working life, "forskudt arbejdstid" means working hours that start at different times (staggered hours).

at forsone sig.explanation: "At forsone sig" means "to reconcile". To name who you make peace with, add "med" (with): "Jeg vil forsone mig med min bror" (I want to reconcile with my brother). To say you accept something hard, use it with the loss: "Han har forsonet sig med tabet" (He has come to terms with the loss).

at forstyrre.explanation: "At forstyrre" means "to disturb". To ask politely when you walk in on someone, say: "Må jeg forstyrre?" (May I interrupt?) To tell someone not to disturb you, say: "Forstyr mig ikke" (Do not disturb me).

at forstå.explanation: "At forstå" means "to understand". To say you do not understand, say: "Jeg forstår ikke" (I do not understand). To say you know a fact, use "at vide" (to know) instead: "Jeg ved, at han kommer" (I know that he is coming).

at forstærke.explanation: "At forstærke" means "to reinforce". It is built from "stærk" (strong). To say you make a wall stronger, say: "Vi forstærker muren" (We reinforce the wall). The device that makes sound louder is "en forstærker" (an amplifier).

at forsvare.explanation: "At forsvare" means "to defend". To say who is defended, put it after the verb: "Soldaterne forsvarer landet" (The soldiers defend the country). In Denmark, the armed forces are called "Forsvaret" (the Defense).

at forsvinde.explanation: "At forsvinde" means "to disappear". To say something that was here is now gone, use "er forsvundet": "Min taske er forsvundet" (My bag has disappeared).

at forsyne.explanation: "At forsyne" means "to supply". To name what you supply, add "med" (with): "Vi forsyner byen med vand" (We supply the city with water). To tell guests at a meal to take food, say: "Forsyn dig!" (Help yourself!)

at forsøge.explanation: "At forsøge" means "to attempt". To say you attempt to do something, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg forsøger at forstå" (I am trying to understand). To say you taste a cake, use "at prøve" (to try) instead: "Jeg prøver kagen" (I try the cake).

at forsømme.explanation: "At forsømme" means "to neglect". To say you let something go without care, put it after the verb: "Han forsømmer sin have" (He neglects his garden). When a student misses lessons, it also fits: "en elev, der forsømmer undervisningen" (a student who skips class).

at forsørge.explanation: "At forsørge" means "to support (financially)". To say who you earn money for, put them after the verb: "Hun forsørger tre børn" (She supports three children). To say you give help or encouragement, use "at støtte" (to support) instead: "Jeg støtter dig" (I support you).

related.en: to feed / provide a living for

at fortage sig.explanation: "At fortage sig" means "to wear off". To say a pain slowly goes away, say: "Smerten fortager sig langsomt" (The pain slowly wears off).

at fortie.explanation: "At fortie" means "to conceal / keep quiet about". To say someone hid a mistake by not mentioning it, say: "Han fortiede fejlen" (He kept the mistake quiet).

at fortjene.explanation: "At fortjene" means "to deserve". To say someone deserves something, put it after the verb: "Du fortjener en pause" (You deserve a break). It is built on "at tjene" (to earn). To say you earn money, use "at tjene" alone: "Jeg tjener penge" (I earn money).

at fortolke.explanation: "At fortolke" means "to interpret". To say a text can be read in different ways, say: "Man kan fortolke et digt på mange måder" (A poem can be read in many ways).

at fortrænge.explanation: "At fortrænge" means "to repress / displace". When you push a painful memory out of your mind, it means "to repress": "Hun har fortrængt ulykken" (She has repressed the accident). When something takes the place of something else, it means "to displace": "Bilen har fortrængt hesten" (The car has displaced the horse).

at fortsætte med.explanation: "At fortsætte med" means "to continue with". To say you carry on with a job, name the job after "med": "Jeg fortsætter med arbejdet" (I continue with the work). To tell someone to keep going, say: "Fortsæt!" (Keep going!)

at fortælle.explanation: "At fortælle" means "to tell". To say you tell someone a story, put the person first: "Jeg fortæller dig en historie" (I am telling you a story). To say someone says a few words aloud, use "at sige" (to say) instead: "Han siger hej" (He says hello).
